name: Retainer wear nightly

lead: Retainers keep a straightened smile straight. After teeth are moved they tend to drift back toward their old positions, and many orthodontists advise nightly wear for years after full-time wear. In looksmaxxing circles it is the way to keep braces or aligner results.

Retainers resist relapse forces from recoil of the periodontal fibres, soft-tissue pressure, the bite and continued growth. Orthodontic sources describe a lifelong risk of relapse, with more than half of patients showing some reversion within 10 years.

paras: Removable types, Hawley or vacuum-formed, are worn at set times, usually overnight; fixed types are wires bonded behind the front teeth. One overview suggests about six months of full-time wear followed by nighttime wear for many years, and the schedule is set by the treating orthodontist.
Poor cleaning can cause plaque, cavities and gum inflammation. Clear retainers worn while eating can trap sugary or acidic substances, and hot water can distort them. Grinding can break them quickly.

angle.text: People who have finished braces or aligners wear retainers at night to keep the straight smile they paid for. The retainer holds tooth positions and limits relapse. Orthodontic sources describe a lifelong relapse risk, with over half of patients showing some reversion within ten years.

lead: Retainers hold teeth in corrected positions after orthodontic treatment. Orthodontic sources state there is a lifelong risk of relapse because of periodontal fibre recoil, soft-tissue pressure, the bite and continued growth [1]. More than 50% of patients show some reversion within 10 years [2].

Removable retainers include Hawley and vacuum-formed types; fixed retainers are wires bonded behind the front teeth. Vacuum-formed retainers are usually worn overnight, and the wear schedule is set by the orthodontist and may be fixed-term or indefinite [1]. One overview suggests about six months of full-time wear followed by nighttime wear for many years [2].

paras: Hawley retainers have a metal wire on an acrylic palate and are adjustable but less attractive and can affect speech. Vacuum-formed retainers are clear plastic shells that are nearly invisible and generally preferred. Fixed retainers depend less on patient cooperation but are harder to clean [1].

A 2020 systematic review cited in the overview found Hawley retainers not effective at preventing incisor irregularity relapse. Vacuum-formed retainers retain lower incisors better than other removable types, and fixed retainers performed best [1]. Compliance is the main practical concern [1].

Poor cleaning can cause plaque, caries and gum inflammation. Vacuum-formed retainers worn while eating, or inserted right after a meal or drink, can trap cariogenic substances; bruxism can break them and hot water can shrink them [1].

Systematic reviews, including a 2016 Cochrane review of retention procedures cited in the overview, have compared retainer types [1]. No studies found specifically on nightly-only wear schedules in the sources reviewed.
